newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline ends higher on supply concerns.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline ends higher on supply concerns.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline ended higher Tuesday on concerns of tight supply, while crude and heating oil ended off slightly in thin volume as traders awaited oil inventory data which has been delayed.
"There is a perception that gasoline supplies are tight. There has been strong buying in the cash markets," said a trader. December gasoline ended 0.75 cent a gallon higher at 65.77 cents.
The American Petroleum Institute (API) was to report its weekly oil inventory data Tuesday evening, but it said it would delay the release of its data until Wednesday afternoon.
An API spokesman said insufficient companies had reported information following Monday's Veteran's Day holiday to produce the report Tuesday.
In the the most recent inventory data, which is for the week ended November 1, gasoline stocks were 6.2 million barrels below year ago and are hovering near record lows.
"The market is going to be looking at the APIs to confirm the move in gasoline," said a trader.
December heating oil ended 0.10 cent a gallon lower at 68.25 cents while December crude settled two cents lower at $23.35 a barrel.
"There was a lot of short covering in the gasoline cracks," said ARB Oil managing director Gerald Samuels.
Besides the crack buying, which entails selling crude for gasoline, crude was pressured by weakness in heating oil.
Heating oil was pressured by forecasts of moderating temperatures for the U.S. Northeast starting Friday, dealers said.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
